newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 28.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- State prosecutors on Monday began investigations into corruption allegations surrounding bank loans to the Hanbo Group. They plan initially to summon 12 people, including Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo.
- Ruling and opposition parties have agreed to launch a parliamentary investigation into Hanbo. Both sides will meet in an emergency session of the National Assembly, possibly as early as February 1.

- Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo said while he would agree to relinquish management rights over Hanbo Steel he would never give up property rights. He also denied allegations of illegal financing for the company.
- North Korea requested a one week delay in a U.S.-South Korea briefing in New York on four-party peace talks. The session was origninally scheduled for January 29.

- President Kim Young-sam ordered Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung to launch a thorough investigation into Hanbo Steel. "A thorough and impartial probe should be made into how Hanbo earned a government license, received loans, and went insolvent," President Kim said.

- Union wokers at Hyundai Motor worked all Saturday and through early Sunday volunatarily to make up for lost production during recent strikes. The overtime work resulted in additional production of 2,900 vehicles, company officials said.

- Non-performing loans are increasing at a dizzying rate. As of the end of November 1996, non-performing loans accounted for 4.7 percent (13.5 trillion won) of total loans. However, if loans to Hanbo Steel go bad, the total amount of non-performing loans will reach nearly 17 trillion won.
